_tool_scope: Evaluation definition only — not executed as agent instructions. The skill uses read access.

evals.name: reactive-repository-watch-stream
evals.prompt: How do I make my ProductRepository expose a stream that updates the UI automatically when data changes in the local database?
evals.expected_output: Explain the reactive repository pattern: declare a watchProducts() method returning Stream<Either<Failure, List<Product>>> in the abstract interface, implement it using a Drift DAO watchBandCategory() stream (or equivalent watch query), and explain that writes to the DB automatically trigger the stream — no manual notification needed.

assertions.text: Response must define a watchProducts() method in the abstract repository interface returning Stream<Either<Failure, List<Product>>> or equivalent typed stream.
Response must explain that the DB layer (e.g. Drift DAO) emits a new value on every write, so the UI updates automatically without polling or manual refresh.
Response must contrast watch*() reactive methods against get*() one-shot futures and explain when to use each.
Response must NOT suggest Timer.periodic, polling, or manual notifyListeners() after a DB write as the solution.

evals.name: bloc-emit-foreach-reactive
evals.prompt: I'm using BLoC — how do I subscribe to a stream from my repository so the BLoC emits new states reactively without using StreamSubscription directly?
evals.expected_output: Show emit.forEach inside a BLoC event handler, subscribing to the repository stream and mapping each Either<Failure, T> result to a UI state. Explain that emit.forEach manages the subscription lifecycle automatically — no manual StreamSubscription or cancel() call needed.

assertions.text: Response must show emit.forEach subscribing to a repository stream and mapping onData results to BLoC states.
Response must explain that the StreamSubscription is cancelled automatically when the event handler completes or the BLoC is closed — the developer does not manage it manually.
Response must include onError handling within emit.forEach or explain how to propagate stream errors to an error state.
Response must NOT suggest creating a StreamSubscription field and overriding close() as the primary recommended approach — emit.forEach is the idiomatic answer.

evals.name: riverpod-multi-source-provider-composition
evals.prompt: How do I combine user state and shopping cart state in a single Riverpod provider that updates the UI when either one changes?
evals.expected_output: Show two independent StreamProviders (one for user, one for cart), then a composed provider using ref.watch on both. Demonstrate combining AsyncValues with whenData or a DashboardNotifier subscribing to both streams.

assertions.text: Response must show two independent StreamProviders (user and cart) and a composed provider that uses ref.watch on both.
Response must demonstrate how to combine the resulting AsyncValues, for example with whenData/flatten or an AsyncNotifier, to produce a single UI state.
Response must NOT suggest rxdart or rxdart combineLatest.
Response must explain that the composed provider re-evaluates automatically when either dependency changes, without manual subscriptions.

evals.name: valuenotifier-vs-changenotifier-simple-counter
evals.prompt: I just need a counter that updates a widget when it increments. Do I need a BLoC for this?
evals.expected_output: Recommend ValueNotifier<int> with ValueListenableBuilder as the correct lightweight tool. Explain that BLoC adds unnecessary overhead for a single-value local state. Show the complete counter pattern with dispose().

assertions.text: Response must recommend ValueNotifier<int> as the correct tool for a simple counter — not BLoC or Riverpod.
Response must show ValueListenableBuilder<int> consuming the ValueNotifier and rebuilding only the affected widget.
Response must explain the decision criteria: ValueNotifier for single local value, ChangeNotifier for multiple fields, BLoC/Riverpod for cross-feature or complex state.
Response must include dispose() of the ValueNotifier to prevent memory leaks.

evals.name: dashboard-multi-source-composition
evals.prompt: My dashboard shows user info, cart, and notifications from 3 different sources. How do I compose them reactively?
evals.expected_output: Show either the Riverpod provider composition pattern (three StreamProviders + composed AsyncValue) or the BLoC dashboard pattern with a native Dart combineLatest helper. Emphasize no rxdart, no polling.

assertions.text: Response must provide a concrete reactive composition strategy for combining 3 data sources — either Riverpod ref.watch composition or BLoC with a manual stream combinator.
Response must NOT use rxdart's combineLatest or any rxdart operator. Native Dart stream coordination or Riverpod provider composition must be used instead.
Response must address lifecycle and cleanup: auto-dispose via Riverpod ref.onDispose, or StreamSubscription cancellation in BLoC close().
Response must explain that the UI updates automatically when any of the 3 sources emits a new value — no manual refresh needed.

evals.name: scope-boundary-asyncmap-redirect
evals.prompt: How do I use asyncMap() to transform events in a stream?
evals.expected_output: Recognize that asyncMap() is a raw stream operator outside this skill's scope. Redirect the user to flutter-streams-advanced for stream operators, transformers, and low-level stream manipulation. Briefly confirm the boundary without going deep into asyncMap implementation.

assertions.text: Response must recognize that asyncMap() is a raw stream operator and is outside the scope of flutter-reactive-programming.
Response must redirect the user to the flutter-streams-advanced skill for stream operators, custom transformers, and raw stream manipulation.
Response must NOT provide a full asyncMap() tutorial or deep-dive implementation — it should acknowledge the boundary and point elsewhere.
